question: Can a fully logged, rerunnable pipeline with a pinned software version reproduce, from the public rdrobust_senate file, the printed default output of Calonico, Cattaneo, Farrell and Titiunik (2017, Sec. 7.2) for the US Senate incumbency advantage (conventional local-linear estimate and robust bias-corrected 95% CI), and how far do the estimate and its falsification checks move across the bandwidth and software choices that the published output leaves open? This is a replication: the estimate and the standard falsification checks on these data are already published (CCFT 2017; Cattaneo, Frandsen and Titiunik 2015), and the paper claims no new finding about the incumbency advantage.
hypotheses: H1 (computational reproduction; targets are the printed values verified by the Scout: conventional estimate 7.416, robust bias-corrected 95% CI [4.094, 10.926], N = 1,297 with h = 17.708): with the rdrobust version pinned in code/requirements.txt and the published defaults (p = 1, triangular kernel, mserd bandwidth, NN variance), each target is reproduced if |replicated - published| <= 0.01 percentage points; N must match exactly. Because H1 holds by construction if the software is deterministic and the version matches, a pass is reported as a computational check, not as evidence about the incumbency advantage. A failure is diagnosed (version, platform), not tuned away.

H2 (falsification, report-only tests fixed now): (a) density test of the margin at 0 with rddensity (default options), robust p-value; (b) each of the four predetermined covariates (termshouse and termssenate are missing for the same 282 rows, so their tests use N = 1,108; the sample is reported for each test) in the seed file (class, termshouse, termssenate, population) as the outcome of the same rdrobust specification, Holm-adjusted over the four at the 5% level; (c) placebo cutoffs at the median of the margin on each side of 0 (one per side), each estimated only on observations on its own side of 0 (margin < 0, margin > 0), reporting N and bandwidth, Holm-adjusted over the two. Each test is reported with its estimate and CI; non-rejection is reported as no evidence of a discontinuity at the stated precision, not as proof of continuity. These four covariates are a subset of the eight in Cattaneo, Frandsen and Titiunik (2015); their p-values are not compared one-to-one with that paper's. The design fixes, before any outcome analysis, the minimum detectable effect (or an equivalence bound) for each test, and the density test's sample and statistic.

H3 (descriptive sensitivity, no decision rule): the estimate and robust CI under the 2014 rdrobust bandwidths (h = 16.79369, b = 27.43745, as printed by CCFT 2017 and verified by the Scout), under half and double the H1 bandwidth h = 17.708, and with p = 2. Reported as a table; not used to change the H1 targets.
contribution: A logged, rerunnable replication of a standard regression-discontinuity estimate with the software version pinned and its falsification checks fixed before any outcome analysis, plus a descriptive account of how much the printed output depends on bandwidth and software defaults. No new claim about the incumbency advantage.

design.summary: A sharp regression-discontinuity replication of the US Senate incumbency advantage: local-linear rdrobust (p = 1, q = 2, triangular kernel, mserd bandwidth, NN variance, robust bias-corrected 95% CI) on the 1,297 elections with an observed outcome, run with rdrobust 2.1.1 (pinned) and masspoints = 'off', the setting that matches the pre-option 2016 release that printed the targets. H1 targets are the printed conventional estimate 7.416, robust CI [4.09441, 10.9255], N = 1,297 and h = 17.708, checked to 0.01 pp and exact N. Falsification checks are fixed in advance: a density test on margin (rddensity, N = 1,390), balance on the four seed covariates (Holm), and one-sided placebo cutoffs (Holm), each with a stated equivalence or power rule; H3 is descriptive sensitivity only.
design.method: H1 (main, run h1-rdrobust): rdrobust(y = vote, x = margin, c = 0, p = 1, q = 2, kernel = 'tri', bwselect = 'mserd', vce = 'nn', nnmatch = 3, level = 95, masspoints = 'off'), no covariates, so covs_drop is inert. Rows with missing vote (93) are dropped by rdrobust, giving N = 1,297 (595 left, 702 right). rd-effect = conventional estimate; rd-ci-low/high = robust bias-corrected CI. Why masspoints = 'off': rdrobust 2.1.1 defaults to 'adjust', which replaces the sample size in the bandwidth selector with the count of unique running-variable values (M = M_l + M_r) and adds bwcheck = 10 when mass points are detected. The margin has mass points only at +100 (38 obs) and -100 (2 obs), none within |margin| <= 30 (dr-checks), so the local estimation sample and the NN variance around the cutoff are unaffected, but the bandwidth formula is not. The 2016 release predates the option; 'off' is therefore the choice that corresponds to its algorithm, fixed here from the package documentation and not from agreement with the printed numbers. H3 reports 'adjust' as a sensitivity row. Tolerances (fixed now): |conventional - 7.416| <= 0.01 pp; each CI endpoint within 0.01 pp of 4.09441 and 10.9255; N exactly 1,297; |h - 17.708| <= 0.0005 (printed to 3 decimals). A failure is diagnosed (version, platform, option) and reported, not tuned. H2(a) density (run h2-density): rddensity(X = margin, c = 0, p = 2, kernel = 'triangular', vce = 'jackknife', bwselect = 'comb', massPoints = True, bino = default) on all 1,390 margins; primary statistic: robust bias-corrected test T_Q and its p-value; conventional T also reported. Margin is outcome-free, so this sample is fixed without reference to vote. H2(b) covariates (run h2-covariates): for each of class, population (N = 1,390) and termshouse, termssenate (N = 1,108, complete cases), rdrobust(y = covariate, x = margin) with exactly the H1 options; robust bias-corrected p-value per covariate, Holm-adjusted over the four at 5%. H2(c) placebo cutoffs (run h2-placebo): c_L = median of margin among margin < 0 and c_R = median of margin among margin > 0, both computed from margin only. Left test: rdrobust(y = vote, x = margin) on margin < 0 only, c = c_L; right test on margin > 0 only, c = c_R; same options as H1; N and selected bandwidth reported for each; Holm over the two. Equivalence and power rules (fixed now, per test): H2(a): the minimum detectable difference in density at 0 (rddensity hat.diff scale, not a log ratio) is (z_0.975 + z_0.80) times the jackknife standard error under the null (the rddensity default vce), computed from margin only in run design-mde (runs/design-mde/metrics.json). Values fixed now: MDE = 0.01136 density units (about 0.52 times the estimated left-side density 0.02169; the density difference is -0.00355, SE 0.00405). Disclosure: run design-mde also recorded the rddensity robust test on margin (T_Q = -0.875, p = 0.381). That is a margin-only statistic, but it was computed before the design gate; the h2-density run will reproduce this specification and this p-value is recorded here, not as a result. H2(b): the minimum detectable covariate effect is (z_0.975 + z_0.80) times that test's own robust standard error (covariate-only, computed in run design-mde). Values fixed now, in covariate units: class MDE 0.401 (N 1,390, robust SE 0.1431); termshouse MDE 1.400 (N 1,108, SE 0.4998); termssenate MDE 2.091 (N 1,108, SE 0.7462); population MDE 2,185,253 persons (N 1,390, SE 780,006). H2(c): equivalence bound of 0.25 SD of vote in the one-sided sample. This is a chosen constant, not a computed MDE: the MDE formula needs the outcome variance, and the design-mde run may not use vote, so no MDE is computed for H2(c). The SD is a descriptive output of the run, not used to choose the bound. A non-rejection is reported as no discontinuity larger than the stated bound at the stated precision, never as proof of continuity. H3 (descriptive, run h3-sensitivity, no decision rule): (i) printed 2014 bandwidths h = 16.79369, b = 27.43745, p = 1, masspoints 'off'; (ii) half of H1 bandwidths, h = 8.854, b = 13.992; (iii) double, h = 35.416, b = 55.968; (iv) p = 2, q = 3, mserd default bandwidth, masspoints 'off'; (v) H1 specification with the 2.1.1 default masspoints = 'adjust'. Baseline for (ii) and (iii) is h = 17.708, b = 27.984. Software: code/requirements.txt pins rdrobust==2.1.1 and rddensity==3.0. Any run that is not one of the listed runs is out of design.
design.data: Source: rdrobust_senate.csv from rdpackages/rdrobust commit 2589686d (sha256 def1fc6b...2ad44; data/manifest.json senate-rd; no licence stated). Unit: a US Senate election, 1914 to 2010, 1,390 rows, 50 states. Running variable margin: Democratic margin of victory at t, percentage points, cutoff 0 (640 negative, 750 positive, no zeros). Outcome vote: Democratic vote share at t+2 for the same seat (93 missing, so N = 1,297 in H1). Covariates: class, termshouse, termssenate, population. termshouse and termssenate are missing for the same 282 rows. Sample restrictions: none beyond rdrobust's removal of missing outcomes; no bandwidth window is imposed beyond the bandwidths the estimator selects. Design checks already run (dr-checks, no vote statistic): the file matches the printed CCFT 2017 Sec. 7.2 moments and counts (32 comparisons). Ties in margin occur only at +/-100, none within |margin| <= 30. Raw data are not committed.
analysis_plan: 1. design-mde (kind data-prep, code/design_mde.py, run id design-mde, runs/design-mde/metrics.json): margin and covariates only; vote is never loaded (outcome_loaded = 0). Logs the H2(a) density MDE (0.01136), the H2(b) covariate MDEs (class 0.401, termshouse 1.400, termssenate 2.091, population 2,185,253) and the margin-only density statistic (T_Q -0.875, p 0.381). Completed before any analysis run.

2. h1-rdrobust (kind analysis, code/h1_replication.py): main specification in the method section. Metrics: conv_coef, conv_se, ci_low, ci_high (robust), h, b, N, N_left, N_right. Claims: rd-effect (conv_coef), rd-ci-low (ci_low), rd-ci-high (ci_high), rd-n (N), rd-bw (h). Also reports the H1 tolerance checks.

3. h2-density (kind analysis, code/h2_density.py): rddensity on margin, N = 1,390. Metrics: T_conv, p_conv, T_Q, p_Q, bandwidth, n_left, n_right. Claim: rd-density-p (p_Q). The same specification was already recorded in design-mde (p = 0.381); the h2-density run reproduces it. Compared with CFT 2015 McCrary p = 0.39 only qualitatively (different test).

4. h2-covariates (kind analysis, code/h2_covariates.py): four rdrobust runs with the H1 options. Metrics per covariate: coef, se, ci_low, ci_high, p_robust, N, h, MDE, plus Holm-adjusted p. Claims: rd-cov-class-p, rd-cov-termshouse-p, rd-cov-termssenate-p, rd-cov-population-p (compared with the printed 0.897, 0.561, 0.901, 0.634 in CCFT 2017 Sec. 7.4, same four covariates).

5. h2-placebo (kind analysis, code/h2_placebo.py): two one-sided rdrobust runs at c_L and c_R on vote. Metrics per side: coef, ci_low, ci_high, p_robust, N, h, Holm p, sd_vote_side. Claims: rd-placebo-left-p, rd-placebo-right-p.

6. h3-sensitivity (kind analysis, code/h3_sensitivity.py): five specifications in the H3 list, reported as one table next to H1; no decision rule. Claims: rd-h3-2014-bw-effect, rd-h3-half-bw-effect, rd-h3-double-bw-effect, rd-h3-p2-effect, rd-h3-adjust-effect.
7. Clean rerun (crew.py rerun) after all runs, against the ledger, to confirm H1 and H2 reproduce. No new estimates.
threats: Software: the printed numbers come from the 2016 release, not rdrobust 2.1.1. H1 may fail for reasons not in the design; the failure is diagnosed by comparing the option set and platform, not by tuning. H1 is a computational check and is not evidence about the incumbency advantage (run h1-rdrobust; H3 rows).

Mass points: masspoints 'off' vs 'adjust' changes the bandwidth through the sample-size term even though ties lie outside every bandwidth in use. Addressed by the fixed choice in H1 and the adjust row in H3 (run h3-sensitivity, row v).

Data fidelity: the CSV comes from the rdrobust repository, not from the .dta used by CCFT. The dr-checks run matches every printed moment and count, but not the outcome values, which are not compared (no vote statistic is allowed before the gate). Addressed by the printed-value check in data/CODEBOOK.md and the H1 targets (run h1-rdrobust).
Covariate set: only four of the eight covariates of CFT 2015 are in the file. The H2(b) tests are not compared one-to-one with CFT 2015 (run h2-covariates).

Non-rejection is weak evidence: density and covariate tests at N = 1,390 may have low power, so the stated MDE and equivalence bounds are reported next to every null result (runs design-mde, h2-density, h2-covariates, h2-placebo).
Multiplicity: Holm across the four covariate tests and across the two placebo tests; the density test is single (runs h2-covariates, h2-placebo).

Missing outcome: 93 elections have no vote. If missingness relates to margin, the H1 sample is not a random subset near the cutoff. Not tested in this design; disclosed as a limitation (run h1-rdrobust reports N by side).

Local estimand: the estimate is local to close elections (bandwidth about 17.7 points). The paper must not call it the incumbency advantage in all elections, as the seed requires. State-clustered inference (CCFT 2017 Sec. 7.4) is not in this plan; it is disclosed rather than added after seeing results.

Placebo bound: the 0.25 SD equivalence bound in H2(c) is a chosen constant, not a computed MDE. The MDE formula needs the outcome variance, which the design does not compute before the gate, so H2(c) has no computed MDE. This is the least grounded part of the design; the PI may object at the gate.

Pre-gate peek: design-mde recorded the margin-only density statistic (p = 0.381) before the design gate. It uses no outcome, but it is a statistic the design had planned to run later. Disclosed here; the h2-density run is fixed to the same specification.

tasks.title: The published estimate (CCFT 2017, Stata Journal 17(2); data of Cattaneo, Frandsen and Titiunik 2015), its exact specification and software version; prior replications and the falsification checks used in that literature

Run fetch-data (data-prep): download rdrobust_senate.csv from the seed URL, verify sha256, record in data/manifest.json with source, licence note, date and hash; prepare-data: data/CODEBOOK.md with variables, N, missingness and ranges of margin and covariates; no statistic of vote by side of the cutoff

Design-stage data checks (data-prep, no vote statistic): ties and mass points in margin; compare the CSV's printed moments for margin, class and population with CCFT 2017 Sec. 7.2 (or other printed descriptive statistics) to establish that the file matches the one used; report in data/CODEBOOK.md
Run design-mde (data-prep, margin and covariate counts only, code/design_mde.py): rddensity null SE and placebo cutoffs c_L, c_R; before any analysis run
Run h1-rdrobust (code/h1_replication.py): main rdrobust specification, pinned 2.1.1, masspoints off; check tolerances; rd-effect, rd-ci-low, rd-ci-high, rd-n, rd-bw
Run h2-density (code/h2_density.py): rddensity on margin, N = 1,390; robust p-value and MDE from design-mde
Run h2-covariates (code/h2_covariates.py): four covariate rdrobust tests with H1 options, N = 1,390 or 1,108, Holm, MDE per test
Run h2-placebo (code/h2_placebo.py): one-sided placebo cutoffs c_L and c_R on vote, Holm, equivalence bound per side
Run h3-sensitivity (code/h3_sensitivity.py): five descriptive specifications next to H1; no decision rule
Write claims.jsonl entries for every reported number, each linked to its run (rd-effect, rd-ci-low, rd-ci-high and the rest of the design list)
Clean rerun (crew.py rerun) after all runs; confirm metrics match the ledger
